newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand runs budget gap of 54 bln baht Oct-Dec.
newsitem.headline: Thailand runs budget gap of 54 bln baht Oct-Dec.

text.p: Thailand said on Monday it ran a budget gap of 53.769 billion baht ($2.08 billion) during the first three months of 1996/97 fiscal year (October-September) compared with a surplus of 16.23 billion baht in the same year-ago period.
The deficit in December alone was 32.487 billion baht, finance ministry data showed.
Revenues collected during the first three months of this fiscal year totalled 168.45 billion baht while the spending was recorded at 222.2 billion baht.

While income tax collections slightly exceeded target, revenues from corporate and trade taxes fell well below the target set by the government due to a slowdown in the economy. The government had aimed to collect revenues worth 186.3 billion baht during October-December.
However, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's government recently launched an austerity program to cut unnecessary spending and insisted that the 1996/97 budget will be balanced.
